summary: Cycle 11 observed: 24 of 27 required residues hold. Three are contradicted: ladders-work (the water-ladder climb), enemies-path (strict count 1 of 3), frame-cost (worst spot 3.73x). Reading the cycle's evidence, and the operator's diagnostic runs outside the store (named as such below; their results are hypotheses here until an in-loop probe repeats them): the ladder failure and the pathing failure both trace to probe placement — the player carried the boat's momentum into a teleport, and in the pathing probe the player left the bait — not to the level. The frame cost is genuine and large: the busiest spot is draw-bound under the software renderer, and the soldiers fighting a god-mode player are most of it.

claims.text: ladders-work: the swimmer was put at x 2583, 13 px from the water ladder at 2570 (inside its 55 px catch), yet in 4 s with W held it went 470 px west to x 2114 and never took the ladder (ladder 0 throughout). The same test passed in cycles 9 and 10 from the same spot, and the shaft climb and the road exit in this very run took their ladder (shaftTop ladder 1). What differs is the test before it: the boat test ends driving west with A held, and put() only zeroes the ragdoll atoms' velocities (labkit.still), not the character's own bodies.

The swimmer's drift is the boat's momentum surviving the teleport: the operator's scratch trail probe (outside the store) put a fresh swimmer at the same ladder six times from 5-45 px off, and it took the ladder and reached the top every time. The probe's put() should still every body (ragdoll atoms and the character's box2d_body, gy, lS), and the water climb should keep a trail so a failure explains itself.

ladders-work's downOk passed on a free fall: the player put on the road over the hatch, S held, ended on the cap at feet -330 with ladder 0 — the probe cannot tell riding the ladder from falling through the hatches. The descent needs a strict test: from beside the hatch, walked onto it with S held, the ladder taken over the hole and kept to its foot (no sample off the ladder between road and cap, no fall speed).

The ladder code itself has a low-frame-rate gap the strict descent would expose: W or S take a ladder only within 28 px of its middle, while a hatch is 140 px wide and a slow frame moves a walker ~60-90 px, so a player walking onto a hatch with S held can be carried past the grab window and fall; the fall catch only applies when nothing is held; and a ladder taken at the catch width (70) is let go the next tick by the 28 px stay check; and left/right held with up/down carries a climber off mid-shaft.

enemies-path: every soldier near the bait (5700, -664) moved 0 px in 20 s — hunters and posts alike, and the patrol crews — while three far soldiers moved (one fell off the cliff, two walked toward the dock). The probe's own shot shows the player's HUD as 'CS PATROL BOAT - DRIVER': the player was not at the bait. The probe hooks only the ragdoll's damage (fire, the CS Heavy's flamethrower 780 px away, does not come through it) and never takes the player out of the boat or checks where it waited; a dead player respawns at the dock, in the boat.

frame-cost: perf (player stood at each spot) gives deck 683 ms / 666 draws, tower span 517, start 633, road 333 against a 183 ms baseline: worst 3.73x. The cycle's breakdown at (8400, -700) is not comparable: perf-breakdown teleports the player without taking it out of the boat, so its asIs/allAsleep/noEnemies steps measured the soldiers near the dock, not the deck.

Where the deck's frame goes (operator's scratch runs outside the store, same session baseline 133 ms): as is 383 ms / 532 draws; every soldier asleep 267 / 352; no enemies 217 / 290; no enemies and no set pieces 167 / 267; half resolution changes little (not fill-bound); no shader programs are linked while measuring; the main thread idles 50-65% (the software rasteriser's draw cost, not script). ThinkNow is 6-9 ms and the render call 15-23 ms of script time. Hiding every soldier's parts for the render saves ~55 ms. So the cost is draw calls — ~0.6-0.8 ms each — from the soldiers (drawn wherever they are) and their fire, and the set pieces (~2 ms each: 23 draws, 50 ms). Even the empty deck is 1.63x the baseline.

Next actions: the staged mod (the review batch plus: ladders — S takes a ladder anywhere over its hatch (60 px), a fast fall is caught whatever is held, a taken ladder holds its climber over the whole hatch, left/right ignored while climbing; characters well off camera hidden for the render only; the cliff tunnel's and the bunker's lower corridor's ceilings raised to 175 px headroom; debug hooks to measure by kind), baked; the play probe (put() stills every body; the water climb with a trail and a swim-in variant; the strict descent; the objective's full hold; respawn time and place; only live crewed patrols counted); the pathing probe (out of the boat, healed every frame, the player's place checked). Next cycle: perf.js made as honest (healed every frame, the player's place checked) and an in-loop frame matrix repeating the scratch measurements.

frame-cost is likely not reachable at 1.5x under the software renderer with the level's fights intact: the empty deck alone measured 1.63x in the operator's run. The remaining reductions (render-time culling of off-camera soldiers, cheaper set pieces) will be measured in-loop first; if the busiest spot stays above 1.5x, the threshold is the human's to decide, not the loop's to move.

unknowns: Whether rifle hunters close 150 px on a player they can already shoot (level 01's did, 600-1000 px); the bait's hunters within the wake window are the flame heavy (780 px), the road trooper (380 px across, 240 up), the deck trooper (200 px).
The frame matrix's numbers are from one scratch session and are noisy (the same state measured 383 and 500 ms); an in-loop run with several windows is needed.
